L181: # Atherton Laboratory
L182: 
L183: ## Our Research
L184: 
L185: We are interested in defining the prognostic and therapeutic role of T cells in hematologic malignancies utilizing a multispecies comparative approach. Our research involves identification and appraisal of novel strategies for T cell-based immunotherapy in clinical trials of canine cancer patients with tumors bearing translational importance for human medicine.
L186: 
L187: 【63†Learn more about our research】
L188: 
L189: * * *
L190: 
L191: ## Clinical Trials
L192: #### Evaluation of Novel CAR T Therapy for Canine Histiocytic Sarcoma
L193: In this study we will investigate the safety and therapeutic activity of a type of engineered white blood cell known as a CAR T cell.  CAR T cells are made from T cells collected from your dog. In this study, we will engineer T cells to express a cancer targeting receptor known as a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR). The CAR directs the modified T cells to the cancer cells which are then killed.
L194: The purpose of this study is to determine the safety of CAR T cells, their maximum tolerated dose, how long they will remain in the patient and their effectiveness against histiocytic sarcoma.
L195: For more information, please email mattath@upenn.edu.

L200: June 7, 2024 | Katie Bardales received ACVIM Resident Research Award for presenting the lab’s studies of the transcriptional immune microenvironment in canine mast cell tumors in Minneapolis. Congratulations, Katie!

L20: # EGFR/HE R2 C anine Cancer Vaccine
L21: 
L22: ​
L23: 
L24: A clinical trial is open at ten locations  for canine patients with osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma and TCC which are cancer types often associated with EGFR/HER2 overexpression.  See 【4†the status page】 to find out which clinics are participating in the study.  Please contact the clinic directly to find out the requirement and to request an appointment.
L25: 
L26: ​
L27: 
L28: Learn more about the potential 【5†benefits of the vaccine including prevention of metastasis here.】
L29: 
L30: ​
L31: 
L32: ​
L33: # Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Combination Therapy
L34: 
L35: ​
L36: 
L37: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (ICI) treatments work by blocking the inhibitory signals that cancer cells use to evade detection by immune cells.
L38: 
L39: 
L40: 
L41: ICI has shown remarkable success in treating various types of cancer in human medicine.
L42: 
L43: 
L44: 
L45: CCA is supporting a number of projects that combine the use of ICI with other immune modulating therapies.
L46: 
L47: ​
L48: 
L49: 【6†Image: Golden Dog†static.wixstatic.com】
L50: 
L51: ​
L52: # Gut Microbiome and Cancer
L53: 
L54: ​
L55: 
L56: With human patients, researchers can now correlate 【7†successful immunotherapy response to the patient's gut microbiome composition】.
L57: This study will analyze the gut microbiome from canine patients receiving immunotherapy treatments at multiple  time points during their treatment.  The ultimate goal is to to be able to help more cancer patients respond to immunotherapy and survive longer through modulation of the microbiome, for example, via diet change or with the help of fecal transplant.
L58: 
L59: 
L60: 
L61: This study is a collaborative effort between Oregon State University, Yale University and private clinics.
L62: 
L63: ​
L64: 
L65: 【8†Image†static.wixstatic.com】
L66: ​
L67: # Fasting and Immune Modulation
L68: 
L69: ​
L70: 
L71: Short term fasting can dramatically relieve the side effects in cancer patients - people ad dogs - undergoing chemotherapy. Cyclic fasting has also been shown to help activate the anti-tumorigenic immune response in human cancer patients. (See this 【9†summary】).  This is the first of a series of studies investigating impact of dietary intervention added to conventional or experimental therapy.
L72: This study is a collaborative effort between Ohio State University and Oregon State University.
L73: 
L74: ​
L75: 
L76: 【10†Image: Dog†static.wixstatic.com】

L78: ​
L79: # CAR-T Therapy for Solid Tumors
L80: 
L81: ​
L82: 
L83: With CAR-T immunotherapy, the patient's T-cells are modified so that they can target cancer cells much more effectively.   The potential of CAR-T therapy has been demonstrated in treating human blood cancers, but not in solid tumors or in canine patients.
L84: This study is exploring how CAR-T therapy targeting B7H3 receptors might be used to treat solid tumors to help canine patients.   A collaborative effort between Northwestern University and University of Illinois teams, 【11†the trial is now enrolling patients with hemangiosarcoma.†vetmed.illinois.edu】
L85: 
L86: ​
L87: ###### Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR)-T therapy works by modifying the immune cells called T cells (a type of white blood cell) to find and fight cancer much more effectively.
L88: 
L89: ​
L90: # Nonspecific Immune Stimulating Therapy
L91: 
L92: ​
L93: 
L94: The ongoing pilot trial is evaluating the efficacy of mycobacterial cell wall fraction (MCWF) - 【12†Immunocidin - in slowing or preventing metastasis of dogs】 with osteosarcoma and other aggressive solid tumors.
L95: 
L96: ​
L97: 
L98: An additional new study for Transitional Cell Carcinoma (Bladder Cancer) canine patients, in collaboration with North Carolina State University, is enrolling canine patients.
L99: 
L100: 【13†Image: Rigsby fibrosarcoma canine patient.png†static.wixstatic.com】
L101: After 1-year old Rigsby was diagnosed with fibrosarcoma, his vet began treating him with Immunocidin as part of a new study.
L102: 
L103: 【14†Image: cytokines and immunotherapy.png†static.wixstatic.com】
L104: # IL-12 Cytokine To Fight Solid Tumors
L105: # ​
L106: Cytokines are powerful molecules that are excreted by immune cells to turn up or turn off the immune system.  But because of potential toxic side-effects,  direct infusion of immune-stimulatory cytokines have not been used.  A team has now figured out a new way to 【15†introduce IL-12 into tumors safely and to induce long-term memory to help prevent recurrence of cancer】.
L107: This work is led by a collaborative team at Northwestern University and University of Missouri and is【16† enrolling ca】【16†nine patients with high-grade soft tissue sarcoma.】
